hypothesis: Fuse the split-KV combine into _attn_fwd_split, but only for short decodes where one CTA can finish it in a single L2 round trip. A new constexpr FUSE is set only when num_splits <= 32 and the split grid is <= 2*SM_count CTAs; on the table that means decode_2048 (16 splits, 128 CTAs) and decode_4096 (32 splits, 256 CTAs). Under FUSE each split CTA stores its fp32 partial and log2 LSE as before, then does a CTA barrier and one acq_rel gpu-scope atomic_add on a per-(batch, packed m-block/KV head) int32 counter. The workspace is cached, zeroed once, and reset by the last CTA. The CTA that sees count == NUM_SPLITS-1 reads all partials of its packed rows with L1-bypassing .cg loads, CR=4 rows at a time as one [CR, BLOCK_S, D] tile, does the exp2 weighting and writes bf16 O. The separate _attn_combine launch is skipped. Decode 8k-64k (64-85 splits) and every other path are unchanged.
rationale: Exp 9 fused the combine everywhere. Its last CTA combined up to 85 splits serially in chunks (~174 KB per KV head, several round trips). That made 8k-64k 2-8 us slower, yet decode_4096 still dropped from 20.48 to 18.72 us, so removing the kernel boundary is worth roughly a timer quantum when the in-kernel combine is cheap. Here the fused path is gated to the shapes where the combine is at most 4 rows x 32 splits x 512 B = 64 KB, loaded in one shot. Those shapes have at most 256 CTAs, so the FUSE variant's higher register count cannot cost occupancy (it is a separate constexpr compilation). The long decodes, where a serial single-CTA combine loses, keep HEAD's two-kernel path. Decode rows carry 7-12 us of fixed cost and are quantized at 2.048 us. Saving one quantum on 2048/4096 is +20%/+11% on those rows.
expected_effect: decode_2048 from ~12.3 to ~10.2-11.3 us and decode_4096 from ~20.5 to ~18.4-19.5 us. All prefill rows and decode 8k-64k are unchanged (same code path: FUSE=False compiles to HEAD's kernel). Geomean +1% to +2.5% if the boundary is worth 1-2 us; neutral otherwise.
